authority_roles.description: Durable project-definition catalog. Owns Project and ProjectSnapshot records and their published policy snapshots.
Profile-definition catalog. Owns WorkProfile and AgentProfile blueprints independently of any live run.
Native owner of an independently addressable Resource. Project and session records only reference or bind it.
Workspace host or runtime that materializes a working environment.
Runtime coordinator for a WorkSession and the bindings, tasks, and artifacts that exist only inside that episode.
Supervisor that owns AgentInstance liveness for a process or endpoint.
Host executor that records RunAttempts and Turns for an assigned run.
Host product that owns HostConversation history. Distinct from work coordination and from protocol connections.
Publishing authority for an Artifact's publication metadata.
Issuer of Principal names. Does not confer authorization by itself.

mappings.notes: Treat this document as a declared correspondence surface, not as an audited crosswalk. Update fidelity to exact or partial only after checking a specific project-interop revision.

HostConversation.notes: Host chat is out of scope for a project-interop definition.

Project.notes: Shared name and likely shared purpose (durable collaboration scope). Unverified.

ProjectSnapshot.notes: Snapshot or export objects may exist; not verified.

model.description: Protocol-neutral semantic interoperability model for agent work. The machine-readable documents under model/ are canonical for terms, relationships, ownership, lifecycle, aliases, mappings, and guidance.
model.name: Agent Work Model

rules.description: Cross-cutting rules that the semantic linter and future generated prose must treat as normative. Distinct owner, lifecycle, cardinality, or failure semantics imply distinct entities and IDs.

rules.statement: Distinct owner, lifecycle, cardinality, or failure semantics imply distinct entities and distinct identity fields.
Unqualified session, agent, and context MUST NOT appear as normative schema field names except in documented compatibility mappings.

Each entity names exactly one catalogued authority role as its owner. Authority roles are external SYSTEM/ROLE boundaries, not the term itself and not another entity. Foreign entities are referenced or observed, not re-owned as a second mutable truth.
Project and ProjectSnapshot MUST NOT contain active runtime state such as PIDs, ports, heartbeats, or current workspaces, runs, or conversations.
ProjectSnapshot is immutable. A project-bound WorkSession pins an exact snapshot revision and does not mutate it.
A WorkSession has zero or more ResourceBindings, AgentRuns, HostConversation attachments, Tasks, and Artifacts.
An AgentRun belongs to exactly one WorkSession and has zero or more RunAttempts and Turns.
An AgentInstance may execute many RunAttempts. Replacing or restarting an instance does not change the AgentRun identity.
Identity fields and handles are names, not authorization.
Credentials MUST NOT be serialized in portable project or session snapshots.
Policy only narrows across trust boundaries. A child binding or run MUST NOT grant more than its parent project or session allows.

Represented inverse relationships and cardinalities MUST agree on both ends. Every declared parent MUST also appear as a matching child relationship to that parent, with the same target, inverse, and cardinality.
Lifecycle transitions MUST reference declared states of the same term.
Identity field names MUST be qualified snake_case names ending in _id, never a bare session, agent, or context token.
identity.field is the index of the term's handle. fields is the exchange shape. The identity field MUST appear exactly once in fields as an identity-kind entry with the same name.

rules.title: Architecture rules

anti_examples: A local checkout directory.
An MCP client connection.
The current Goose or Crush chat transcript.
A running agent process.

authority.notes: The project-catalog role is the sole mutable authority for project policy and membership.

terms.definition: A durable named collaboration and policy scope. A Project outlives any single workspace, host conversation, or WorkSession and is the unit that people and systems recognize as "the work we keep doing together."
examples: A named product effort that several WorkSessions and hosts attach to over months.
An interoperability profile shared by multiple agent systems under one policy.

fields.name: policy
fields.notes: Policy at the project boundary. Children may only narrow it.

invariants.text: A Project MUST NOT store PIDs, ports, heartbeats, or current run/workspace/conversation pointers.
Project policy and membership have exactly one mutable authority, the Project itself.
Any WorkSession or ResourceBinding under this Project MUST only narrow project policy.
A Project MUST NOT be treated as a Workspace or WorkSession.

transitions.notes: Archiving retains identity and snapshots; it does not delete history.

project-interop.notes: Name alignment is likely; treat field-level equivalence as unverified.

non_synonyms.reason: A Workspace is a material working environment, not the durable collaboration scope.
A WorkSession is a bounded episode; a Project outlives many sessions.
A version-control repository may be a Resource bound into work; it is not the Project.
Unqualified session is prohibited; it collapses several distinct entities.

terms.purpose: Hold stable identity, membership, and policy that WorkSessions pin via a ProjectSnapshot. Projects are not a place to store live runtime.

relationships.name: snapshots
relationships.notes: Every snapshot is a frozen revision of this project.

relationships.name: known_resources
relationships.notes: Observation only. The Project does not become a second owner of the Resource.

anti_examples: A live project record that still accepts policy edits.
A bundle that includes API tokens or raw credentials.

authority.notes: The project-catalog role publishes snapshots as append-only. Corrections produce a new snapshot, never an edit.

terms.definition: An immutable resolved project definition at an exact revision. It is the pinned meaning of a Project that a WorkSession actually ran against.
examples: Hash-addressed export of project policy and resource names used to open a WorkSession.

fields.name: revision
fields.notes: Exact revision identifier of the resolved definition.

fields.name: resolved_definition
fields.notes: Must not embed credentials or live runtime handles.

invariants.text: A ProjectSnapshot MUST be immutable after publication.
A ProjectSnapshot MUST NOT contain PIDs, ports, heartbeats, or current workspace/run/conversation state.
A ProjectSnapshot MUST NOT serialize credentials or other secrets.
A project-bound WorkSession MUST pin exactly one ProjectSnapshot revision.

project-interop.notes: Snapshot/export objects may exist; equivalence is unverified.

non_synonyms.reason: The live Project remains mutable; the snapshot is a frozen revision.
A snapshot is definition, not an episode of work.

terms.purpose: Give WorkSessions a frozen, portable project definition so later mutation of the live Project cannot rewrite history.

anti_examples: The currently open review being performed by an agent.

authority.notes: The profile-catalog role is the sole mutable authority for the work blueprint.

terms.definition: A reusable blueprint for a kind of WorkSession. It describes intended participants, resource shapes, and task patterns without being a live episode of work.
examples: A "code review" blueprint reused every time a review WorkSession is opened.

invariants.text: A WorkProfile MUST NOT be treated as a live WorkSession or as runtime state.
A WorkProfile SHOULD be reusable across many WorkSessions.

non_synonyms.reason: The profile is a template; the session is a bounded episode created from it.
AgentProfile describes an eligible kind of agent, not a kind of work episode.

terms.purpose: Let teams open many similar WorkSessions from one declared template without copying ad-hoc session configuration.

anti_examples: An ephemeral in-memory retrieval blob with no address.
A capability token (that is a credential, not a Resource identity).

authority.notes: The native-resource-provider role remains authoritative. Project and session records only reference or bind the Resource.

terms.definition: An independently addressable thing relevant to work. A Resource is not necessarily owned by a Project; projects and sessions observe or bind it.
examples: A git repository URL.
A dataset catalog entry.
A ticket project that several WorkSessions consult.

invariants.text: A Resource MUST remain independently addressable outside any one Project.
A ResourceBinding MUST NOT become the mutable authority for the Resource.
resource_id and uri are names. They do not grant access.

non_synonyms.reason: The binding is a session-specific grant and resolution, not the thing itself.
An Artifact is an output published by work, not an independently existing resource.
Workspace is a Resource subtype, not a synonym for every Resource.

terms.purpose: Name the durable thing (repository, dataset, ticket tracker, workspace environment, secret store) that bindings and policies talk about.

relationships.name: workspace_form
relationships.notes: Present when this resource is (or specializes as) a Workspace.

anti_examples: Copying the repository's mutable metadata into the session as a second source of truth.

authority.notes: The work-session-coordinator role is the sole mutable authority for this session grant, not for the Resource.

terms.definition: A WorkSession-specific resolution and grant for a Resource. The binding records how this session names, locates, and is allowed to use the Resource without becoming a second owner of it.
examples: Granting a WorkSession read-only access to a named repository at a pinned locator.

fields.name: grant
fields.notes: Must be a narrowing of session and project policy.

fields.name: resolved_locator
fields.notes: How this session locates the resource. Not a credential.

invariants.text: A ResourceBinding MUST belong to exactly one WorkSession.
A binding grant MUST NOT exceed the WorkSession or Project policy.
A ResourceBinding MUST NOT claim mutable authority over the Resource.
A portable binding MUST NOT serialize credentials.

non_synonyms.reason: The resource exists independently of any one session binding.
A Workspace may be the bound resource; the binding is the grant, not the environment.

terms.purpose: Attach a Resource to one WorkSession with a narrowed grant, leaving the Resource's native authority intact.

anti_examples: The host product's chat transcript.
An MCP stdio connection.

authority.notes: The workspace-provider role is the mutable authority for the Workspace environment.

terms.definition: A Resource subtype that provides a material working environment (files, checkout, container, or equivalent). A Workspace is not a WorkSession.
examples: A git worktree used by one WorkSession.
A container filesystem mounted for an AgentRun.

invariants.text: A Workspace MUST be independently addressable as a Resource.
A Workspace MUST NOT be treated as a WorkSession or as an MCP connection.
A Workspace MUST NOT be treated as the Project.

non_synonyms.reason: The session coordinates work; the workspace is one bound environment.
The project is the durable policy scope, not a checkout or container.
Chat history is not a working environment.

terms.purpose: Name the environment in which work is performed so it can be bound into a WorkSession without being confused with the episode of work itself.

relationships.name: bound_in
relationships.notes: Bindings attach the workspace into WorkSessions; they do not own it.

anti_examples: A Crush or Goose chat thread taken as the work itself.
An MCP transport connection or a historical Mcp-Session-Id.
A durable Project.

authority.notes: The work-session-coordinator role is the sole mutable authority for the episode graph.

terms.definition: A bounded episode of work that coordinates resources and participants. A WorkSession may contain many AgentRuns and ResourceBindings. It is never an MCP connection and never a host chat transcript.
examples: A time-bounded incident response that several agents and a human join.
A multi-hour implementation episode pinning one ProjectSnapshot.

fields.name: policy
fields.notes: Must only narrow the pinned ProjectSnapshot policy.

invariants.text: A project-bound WorkSession MUST pin exactly one ProjectSnapshot revision.
A WorkSession MUST allow 0..* ResourceBindings, AgentRuns, HostConversation attachments, Tasks, and Artifacts.
A WorkSession MUST NOT be identified with an MCP connection or transport session.
A WorkSession MUST NOT be identified with a HostConversation.
A portable WorkSession snapshot MUST NOT serialize credentials.
WorkSession policy MUST only narrow the pinned project policy.

non_synonyms.reason: Host chat history may attach to a session; it is not the session.
An AgentRun is one agent's assignment inside the session.
A workspace is a bound environment, not the coordinating episode.
MCP 2026-07-28 has no protocol-level session; historical transport identifiers are not work episodes.

terms.purpose: Be the unit that binds a ProjectSnapshot, resources, tasks, artifacts, conversations, and agent assignments into one episode with a start and an end.

relationships.name: project_snapshot
relationships.notes: Project-bound sessions pin an exact snapshot revision.

anti_examples: A PID of a currently running agent process.

authority.notes: The profile-catalog role is the sole mutable authority for the agent kind.

terms.definition: A declarative description of an eligible kind of agent. It names capabilities, constraints, and intended roles without identifying a running process.
examples: A "repository reviewer" profile reused across many AgentRuns.

invariants.text: An AgentProfile MUST NOT be treated as a running AgentInstance.
An AgentProfile MUST NOT be treated as an AgentRun.

non_synonyms.reason: The instance is a running process or endpoint, not the declared kind.
The run is a bounded assignment, not a reusable kind.
A principal is an authenticated identity, which a profile is not.

terms.purpose: Select and constrain which kinds of agents may be assigned to AgentRuns without confusing the kind with a live instance or an assignment.

anti_examples: The logical assignment "review PR 42" (that is an AgentRun or Task).

authority.notes: The agent-runtime role is the authority for liveness of this process or endpoint.

terms.definition: A running process or remote endpoint capable of executing RunAttempts. An AgentInstance is not an assignment and is not a Principal.
examples: A local agent process that executes several RunAttempts and is then replaced.
A remote agent endpoint that picks up attempts for more than one AgentRun.

fields.name: agent_instance_id
fields.notes: Instance identity is not required in portable project snapshots.

invariants.text: An AgentInstance MAY execute many RunAttempts, including for different AgentRuns.
Replacing or restarting an AgentInstance MUST NOT change an AgentRun identity.
An AgentInstance MUST NOT be treated as an AgentRun.
An AgentInstance MUST NOT be treated as the authenticated Principal.

non_synonyms.reason: The run is the assignment; the instance is the executor.
The profile is the kind; the instance is a live process or endpoint.
Identity for auth is Principal; the instance is infrastructure.

terms.purpose: Name the live executor that performs attempts so that replacing or restarting it does not rewrite the AgentRun identity.

relationships.name: principal
relationships.notes: The instance may present a Principal; it is not itself the Principal.

anti_examples: Calling the host chat an "agent session".
Re-identifying the assignment when the process is restarted.

authority.notes: The work-session-coordinator role is the sole mutable authority for the assignment.

terms.definition: One agent's bounded assignment within exactly one WorkSession. An AgentRun may contain Turns and RunAttempts. This is the accepted term that replaces the ambiguous phrase "agent session".
examples: Assigning one reviewer agent to a WorkSession to produce a review Artifact.

invariants.text: An AgentRun MUST belong to exactly one WorkSession.
An AgentRun MUST allow 0..* RunAttempts and 0..* Turns.
Replacing or restarting an AgentInstance MUST NOT change agent_run_id.
Implementations MUST NOT use unqualified "agent session" as the name of this entity.
An AgentRun MUST only receive grants that narrow WorkSession policy.

non_synonyms.reason: The session may contain many AgentRuns.
The instance executes attempts; it is not the assignment.
An attempt is one infrastructure execution of the run.
A turn is one input-to-output cycle inside the run.
A task is a schedulable graph node and is not necessarily 1:1 with a run.
Host chat is not an agent assignment.

terms.purpose: Record the assignment, its outcomes, and the attempts and turns that fulfilled it, independently of which AgentInstance executed them.

relationships.name: tasks
relationships.notes: A Task is not necessarily 1:1 with an AgentRun.

anti_examples: Minting a new AgentRun because the process crashed.

authority.notes: The agent-executor role is the authority for this execution try.

terms.definition: One infrastructure execution attempt for an AgentRun. Failures, retries, and instance replacements produce new RunAttempts under the same AgentRun.
examples: Retrying a failed launch on a replacement AgentInstance under the same agent_run_id.

invariants.text: A RunAttempt MUST belong to exactly one AgentRun.
A later RunAttempt MAY be executed by a different AgentInstance than an earlier one.
A RunAttempt MUST NOT replace the AgentRun identity.

non_synonyms.reason: The run is the assignment; the attempt is one try at executing it.
Turns are conversational or control cycles, not infrastructure launches.
The instance is the executor, not the attempt record.

terms.purpose: Separate retry and crash semantics from the logical assignment so an AgentRun can survive executor replacement.

anti_examples: The entire Goose or Crush transcript.

authority.notes: The agent-executor role is the authority for this cycle.

terms.definition: One input-to-output or control-yield cycle inside an AgentRun. A Turn is smaller than a RunAttempt and is not a HostConversation.
examples: One model invocation that yields a tool call and later completes.

invariants.text: A Turn MUST belong to exactly one AgentRun.
A Turn MUST NOT be treated as a HostConversation.
A Turn MUST NOT be treated as a RunAttempt.

non_synonyms.reason: Host chat is owned by the host product and may span or omit turns.
An attempt is an infrastructure execution, not one I/O cycle.
A run contains many turns.

terms.purpose: Account for the conversational or control steps that make up an AgentRun without collapsing them into host chat or infrastructure attempts.

anti_examples: Calling the host chat the WorkSession.
Using MCP connection identity as the conversation identity.

authority.notes: The host-product role is the mutable authority for this conversation history.

terms.definition: Conversation history owned by a host product such as Goose, Hermes, or Crush. A HostConversation may attach to a WorkSession but is not the WorkSession.
examples: A Goose conversation that a user later attaches to an existing WorkSession.
A Crush chat that never attaches to any WorkSession.

fields.name: host_system
fields.notes: Name of the owning host product.

invariants.text: A HostConversation MUST remain owned by its host product.
A HostConversation MUST NOT be treated as a WorkSession.
A HostConversation MUST NOT be treated as an AgentRun.
A HostConversation SHOULD be attachable to at most one WorkSession.

non_synonyms.reason: The session is the work episode; the conversation is host-owned history.
Turns live inside an AgentRun; host messages may not map 1:1.
An assignment is not a chat transcript.

terms.purpose: Keep host-owned chat history distinct from the work episode, the assignment, and individual turns so products can attach transcripts without becoming the model.

anti_examples: Equating every AgentRun with exactly one Task.

authority.notes: The work-session-coordinator role is the authority for this task graph node.

terms.definition: A schedulable unit in a WorkSession task graph. A Task is not necessarily one-to-one with an AgentRun.
examples: A "draft the migration plan" node that two AgentRuns later serve.

invariants.text: A Task MUST belong to exactly one WorkSession.
A Task MUST NOT be assumed to map 1:1 to an AgentRun.

non_synonyms.reason: Several runs may serve one task, or one run may serve several tasks.
An artifact is an output, not the schedulable unit.
A turn is a cycle inside a run, not a graph node.

terms.purpose: Describe planned or in-flight work items and their dependencies without forcing each item to be an agent assignment.

anti_examples: Hidden chain-of-thought.
An unpublished scratch file in a workspace.

authority.notes: The artifact-publisher role is the authority for publication metadata, not for private reasoning.

terms.definition: A durable explicit output published by a Task or AgentRun. An Artifact is not private reasoning, scratch, or an unpublished tool side effect.
examples: A review report written to an agreed locator and attached to the WorkSession.

fields.name: locator
fields.notes: Address of the published bytes. Not a credential.

invariants.text: An Artifact MUST be an explicit published output, not private reasoning.
An Artifact SHOULD record the Task and/or AgentRun that published it.
An Artifact locator MUST NOT embed credentials.

non_synonyms.reason: A resource exists independently; an artifact is produced by work.
Intermediate model text is not an artifact until published.
The task is the plan node; the artifact is the output.

terms.purpose: Name the things a session intends to keep and share so they can be addressed independently of turns and attempts.

anti_examples: A PID.
An API token stored in a snapshot.

authority.notes: The identity-provider role is the authority for the Principal name. It does not confer authorization.

terms.definition: An authenticated human, service, or agent identity. A Principal is not an AgentInstance and is not an assignment.
examples: A human user identity that opens a WorkSession.
A service identity that an AgentInstance presents.

fields.name: kind
fields.notes: human, service, or agent identity kind.

invariants.text: principal_id is a name. Authorization is decided by policy, not by possessing the identifier.
A Principal MUST NOT be treated as an AgentInstance.
A portable snapshot MUST NOT include the Principal's credentials.

non_synonyms.reason: The instance is a process or endpoint that may present a Principal.
The run is an assignment given to a Principal or performed via an instance.
The profile is a kind, not an authenticated identity.

terms.purpose: Be the subject of authentication and authorization so process identity and work assignment stay separate from who is acting.
